verdict.summary: You can build a public GitHub App for each customer's repositories. Normal setup takes hours and does not require GitHub approval. During installation, the user or organization owner approves the requested permissions and selects repositories.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours, mostly building secure authorization and webhook handling
verdict.waitTime: No provider review is required for normal GitHub App registration.
verdict.mainGate: During each installation, the user or organization owner must approve the app's requested permissions and choose its repositories.

recommendation.text: Use a public GitHub App. Choose Any account so each customer can install it. Use installation tokens for background work and user tokens for attributed actions.

sources.quote: If you want to access GitHub resources on behalf of a user or in an organization, or you anticipate a long-lived integration, we recommend building a GitHub App.
OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user while GitHub Apps can either act on behalf of a user or independently of a user.
Under ‘Where can this GitHub App be installed?’, select Only on this account or Any account.

essentials.text: User tokens expire after 8 hours. Request offline_access for refresh tokens. Refresh tokens expire after six months and rotate after use.

sources.quote: By default, the user access token expires after 8 hours.
To receive an expiring user access token and a refresh token for this authorization, set this value to offline_access.
The user access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months.
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.

essentials.text: Register exact HTTPS callback URLs. GitHub Apps allow up to 10 callback URLs. Do not enable wildcard matching for customer-controlled paths.

sources.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
up to 10 callback URLs.
Enabling wildcard matching can expose your app to security risks, because it allows an attacker to send authorization codes to any subdomain or subdirectory of the callback URL.

essentials.text: Create a separate public development app with matching settings. Use a draft Marketplace listing for billing tests without real charges.

sources.quote: we recommend configuring a separate development app, with the same configuration as your production app
Any purchases you make using a draft GitHub Marketplace listing will not create real transactions, and GitHub will not charge your credit card.

15,000 requests per hour.

essentials.text: Use state and PKCE S256 during user authorization. Verify webhook HMAC signatures over raw request bytes. Store keys and tokens in encrypted server-side storage.

sources.quote: When specified, the value should contain a random string to protect against forgery attacks.
Strongly recommended
Must be S256 - the plain code challenge method is not supported.
The hash signature will appear in each delivery as the value of the X-Hub-Signature-256 header.
Never use a plain == operator.
Never hardcode a token into an application or push a token to any repository.

requests.text: For GitHub Apps, offline_access is the only supported scope and requests an expiring token with a refresh token.

sources.quote: Direct the user to this URL, and add any necessary query parameters from the following list of parameters: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize .
scope string Optional To receive an expiring user access token and a refresh token for this authorization, set this value to offline_access . No other scopes are supported for GitHub Apps.
code_challenge string Strongly recommended Used to secure the authentication flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange).

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the callback code for a user access token and, with offline_access, a refresh token.

sources.quote: Exchange the code from the previous step for a user access token by making a POST request to this URL, along with the following query parameters: https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
code_verifier string Strongly recommended. Used to secure the authentication flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange). Required if code_challenge was sent during the user authorization.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: Refresh tokens are single-use; using one invalidates it and the old access token.

sources.quote: Make a POST request to this URL, along with the following query parameters: https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
grant_type string Required. The value must be "refresh_token".
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.

detail.text: Do not submit anything for normal GitHub App installation. Marketplace publication is optional for discovery or GitHub-billed plans. If you choose Marketplace, first meet its listing requirements and request publication. For paid Marketplace plans, the publisher must be verified and complete financial onboarding. The app needs at least 100 installations, and an app owned by a personal account must be transferred to an organization. Paid plans must offer monthly and annual prices and handle Marketplace billing events, including purchases, upgrades, downgrades, cancellations, and trials. After you click Request publish, an onboarding expert will contact you.

sources.quote: click Request publish.

detail.text: Read rate-limit headers and queue retries with backoff. Keep work separate per customer installation. Never pool tokens to bypass limits.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps authenticating with an installation access token use the installation's minimum rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
You may not share API tokens to exceed GitHub's rate limitations.
